question: Should exact requester consumption permanently satisfy descendant delivery even when the requester’s final outward send later fails?
rationale: This intentionally suppresses later descendant delivery retry and changes durable lifecycle state; tests can establish consistency but cannot choose the product delivery boundary.

options.title: Require proof and accept the boundary
options.body: Accept requester consumption as terminal descendant delivery after redacted real cron/background restart proof confirms consumed rows remain delivered and unconsumed rows remain retryable.

options.title: Require outward delivery
options.body: Keep descendant delivery pending until the requester result is successfully delivered outward, preserving descendant retry when the requester send fails.

options.title: Fold into durable inbox work
options.body: Pause this patch and resolve requester-consumed accounting as part of the broader durable completion inbox or spool design.

recommendation.title: Require proof and accept the boundary
recommendation.body: Accept requester consumption as terminal descendant delivery after redacted real cron/background restart proof confirms consumed rows remain delivered and unconsumed rows remain retryable.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged descendant-gating work is the closest feature-history ownership signal for deciding the terminal announcement and delivery invariant.
